<objective>
Make the per-task wall-clock cap real in production, and give the production runner the database handle it
needs to record its own terminal reasons by their actual kind.

Purpose: `02-VERIFICATION.md` found both of these built-but-unreached. `tasks.wall_clock_cap_ms` is resolved
per task through the full task > `.fleet.yml` > Fleet config > default order and persisted on every row — and
then never read back. `RunnerTask` has no field for it, so `Scheduler.dispatch()` cannot pass it, so every
task in production is killed at exactly the hardcoded 30-minute default no matter what its row says. The
safety property survives (a hang is genuinely killed); the "overridable per task" property D-11 and ROADMAP
Success Criterion 2 both claim does not. Separately, `buildApp()` constructs the production runner without a
database handle, so the runner's own typed reasons — the wall-clock timeout and the `apiKeySource`
violation — are lost and the task lands in `failed` carrying only the Scheduler's generic reason.

Output: a `wallClockCapMs` field on the `Runner` seam, populated from the task row, feeding the timer that
actually fires; a resolution ceiling that refuses a cap too large for a Node timer to represent; and a
production runner wired to the event store through the phase's single write path and no other.
</objective>

  <action>
Close the break at hop three of the cap chain.

**`src/runner/runner.interface.ts`** — add `wallClockCapMs: number` to `RunnerTask`, immediately after
`maxTurns` so the two caps sit together. Type it as a required `number`, not a nullable one: `createTask`
already resolves and persists a concrete value on every row, so "the runner was handed no cap" is a bug the
type system should make unrepresentable rather than a case the runner has to re-default at spawn time.
Extend the field's doc comment in the voice of the existing `agentProfileName` comment, recording that the
value is the ALREADY-RESOLVED one from the task row — the runner does not re-run the task/`.fleet.yml`/config
precedence, it receives its outcome, which is what keeps a future container backend able to satisfy the same
seam without importing Fleet's config readers.

**`src/runner/worktree-runner.ts`** — three changes.

First, add an exported `MAX_WALL_CLOCK_CAP_MS` constant equal to the largest delay a Node timer represents
without overflow (2147483647). Record in its doc comment WHY it exists: a `setTimeout` delay above that
value does not produce a long timer, it fires on the next tick — which would silently convert this phase's
safety backstop into an immediate kill of every task carrying such a cap. This is the RUN-03 precision edge:
the failure is not a rejected value, it is a value that appears accepted and inverts the behaviour.

Second, extend `resolveOneCap`'s validation so a `wallClockCapMs` above `MAX_WALL_CLOCK_CAP_MS` throws a
`CapsError` naming the layer, the field, the offending value, and the ceiling. Keep the existing
positive-integer rule exactly as it is — an explicit `0` stays a genuine invalid value and is never treated
as inherit. Apply the ceiling to the wall-clock field specifically rather than to every cap: a max-turns
value has no timer behind it and no such inversion.

Third, in `spawn()`, replace the sole `resolveCaps({ task: this.options.caps })` input with one that takes
the task row's already-resolved value as the TASK layer and demotes the runner-construction-time
`WorktreeRunnerOptions.caps` to a lower layer. Concretely: the task layer supplies `wallClockCapMs` from
`task.wallClockCapMs` and `maxTurns` from `task.maxTurns`, and `this.options.caps` becomes the `config`
layer. That ordering is the whole point — the per-task value must win over an instance-wide one, or this
plan closes nothing. Update `WorktreeRunnerOptions.caps`'s doc comment: delete the paragraph recording that
`RunnerTask` does not yet carry `wallClockCapMs` and that widening the seam was out of the owning plan's
file scope, and replace it with what the option now means — an instance-wide fallback, retained so a caller
constructing its own runner can set a floor without a task row.

**`src/scheduler/queue.ts`** — in `dispatch()`'s `RunnerTask` assembly, populate `wallClockCapMs` from
`taskRow.wallClockCapMs`, falling back to the same built-in default the runner exports, mirroring the
existing `maxTurns` line exactly. Import the default from the runner module rather than declaring a third
copy of the number — `queue.ts` already declares its own `DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS`, and this plan should not add a
second instance of that same duplication. Also populate `wallClockCapMs` on the `RunnerTask` that
`tasks/service.ts`'s `cancelTask` builds if the type change makes that construction fail to compile; that
object is only ever passed to `kill()` and never spawns, so the built-in default is the correct value there
and the comment already present for `agentProfileName` is the model for saying so.

**`src/runner/worktree-runner.test.ts`** — add the boundary and precision cases from `<behavior>` to the
existing `resolveCaps` describe block, and extend the shared precedence assertions so the wall-clock cap is
driven through the same table the model and max-turns resolvers already share. Do not write a second,
parallel precedence table for it.
  </action>
